policy.purpose: A small, source-attributed catalog of independently worded shot patterns for the local PS4 AI Video Studio workflow.
policy.githubMaterial: The pinned official higgsfield-ai/skills repository is MIT-licensed. Preserve its copyright and license notice when copying substantial portions.
policy.websiteMaterial: Higgsfield Academy, blog, prompt-bank, and static assets are reference-only because no redistribution license was found on those pages.
policy.commercialUseConclusion: Use the project-authored templates below or properly attributed MIT material. Do not redistribute Higgsfield-authored website prompts, images, videos, course files, or shotlists without separate permission.

patterns.goal: Turn one surprising factual question into a compact aspect-aware visual arc.
patterns.derivation: Independent wording based on general subject/action/setting/camera guidance; no website prompt text is copied.
patterns.template: Aspect {aspectRatio}, {durationSeconds} seconds. Open close on {surprisingDetail} in {setting}. Let {proofAction} supply the visible evidence while the camera performs one {cameraMove}. End on a stable proof frame. Use {lighting}. Keep generated sound to {ambientAudio}; narration and captions are added later.
guardrails: Use one verifiable claim per clip.
Show evidence rather than displaying generated text.
Use original, unbranded subjects and locations unless rights are documented.
Keep narration out of the generated clip so the local mixer controls timing.

patterns.goal: Make a physical change easy to compare without camera drift.
patterns.derivation: Original camera-direction wording informed by the public camera-movement taxonomy and MIT prompt guidance.
patterns.template: A {shotScale} view of {subject} in {setting}. The camera remains fixed on a firm tripod and the composition stays unchanged from first frame to last. All visible motion comes from {action}. Use {lighting} and {ambientAudio}.
guardrails: Keep lens, horizon, distance, and framing constant.
Reserve the last beat for a readable comparison frame.
Avoid logos, watermarks, and generated on-screen copy.

patterns.goal: Reveal the answer by rotating from a clue to its context.
patterns.derivation: Independent description of a standard pan; no prompt-bank phrasing is reproduced.
patterns.template: Begin on {openingClue}. From a fixed camera position, rotate smoothly toward screen {direction} across {environment} at {speed} speed. Land on {landingSubject}, ease to a stop, and hold the final composition for {endHoldSeconds} seconds.
guardrails: Use rotation only; keep the camera position and horizon stable.
Do not combine the pan with a zoom or lateral track.
Time the reveal to the narration payoff.

patterns.goal: Use real perspective change to turn an architectural detail into a reveal.
patterns.derivation: Original formulation of a standard dolly move informed by official educational references.
patterns.template: Track physically forward toward {subject}, moving from {startDistance} to {endDistance} with a fixed {lens} lens at {movementSpeed} speed. Let {foregroundLayers} pass with clear parallax. Ease into a still final frame on the key detail.
guardrails: Keep focal length fixed so the move reads as a dolly rather than a zoom.
Use one continuous path without orbiting or tilting.
Keep the subject readable throughout the approach.

patterns.goal: Keep a moving subject legible while spatial layers demonstrate scale or construction.
patterns.derivation: Independent wording for a standard tracking shot, with no copied prompt-bank text.
patterns.template: Move laterally beside {subject} as it {subjectAction}, matching its {speed} pace so its size remains steady. Build three depth layers: {nearLayer} crossing fastest, {middleLayer} moving with the subject, and {farLayer} drifting slowest.
guardrails: Maintain a consistent side angle and subject scale.
Use foreground occlusion briefly, never long enough to hide the evidence.
Keep the camera path parallel to the subject.

patterns.goal: Transfer attention from a contextual clue to the detail that answers the question.
patterns.derivation: Original description of a standard rack-focus technique.
patterns.template: Lock the camera composition. Hold sharp focus on {contextPlane} for {holdBeforeSeconds} seconds, shift focus once over {focusShiftSeconds} seconds to {evidencePlane}, then hold the evidence sharp for {holdAfterSeconds} seconds while the first plane falls softly out of focus.
guardrails: Change focus only; keep position, framing, and focal length stable.
Use one deliberate focus transfer without hunting.
Match the transfer to a single narration transition.

patterns.goal: Keep independently generated clips visually compatible for unattended assembly.
patterns.derivation: Project-authored continuity contract based on the MIT source's shared-style principle and the public guide's shot-structure concept.
patterns.template: Apply this unchanged continuity contract to every segment: aspect {aspectRatio}; palette {palette}; key light {lightingDirection}; lens family {lensFamily}; finish {texture}; recurring subject definition {subjectIdentity}; generated audio policy {audioPolicy}. Each segment adds only its own action and camera move.
guardrails: Store the exact contract and its hash in every segment receipt.
Change one variable at a time during retries.
Reuse only project-owned or properly licensed references.
Do not use a real person's likeness without documented consent.

patterns.goal: Create deterministic narration, visual, and caption alignment across a multi-clip short.
patterns.derivation: Independently worded implementation pattern adapted from the official MIT explainer workflow.
patterns.template: Block {blockIndex}, {durationSeconds} seconds. Narration source: {narrationLine}. Show one matching action: {visualAction}. Camera: {cameraMove}. Generate only {ambientAudio}; speech and timed captions are assembled from the narration source after video generation.
guardrails: Bind exactly one narration take, one clip, and one caption cue group to each block index.
Generate narration before final caption timing.
Reject missing, duplicate, or out-of-order block identifiers.
Keep visual claims within the cited factual source material.
